The system evaluates whether evidence meets criteria for ACTIVE, SHADOW_ONLY, or BLOCKED status. When evidence is stale or untrusted, it blocks downstream model components such as 'model.trueEv', which requires a specific edge-lab verdict to activate. This introduces a dual-layered constraint: one from data quality and another from logical consistency. The system models failure modes through explicit blocking rules rather than probabilistic collapse. Trust normalization ensures uniformity across different source types. The matrix acts as a decision filter for model inference, enforcing integrity checks before allowing evidence to contribute to a score.
